title: Three algorithms behind one interface
note: k-means (spherical clusters), Gaussian mixture (elliptical, soft assignments) and Ward hierarchical clustering share one function, so the tournament can compare them without special cases.

title: Bootstrap stability
note: Resample customers with replacement, refit, and compare the new labels with the full-data labels on the shared customers using the Adjusted Rand Index (label-permutation invariant). A real segment structure survives resampling; noise does not.

title: The tournament
note: Every feature set × algorithm × k is scored on silhouette and stability. DBSCAN joins with an eps sweep (it chooses k itself). Configs with a cluster under 8 customers are dropped as not actionable, then ranked by an equal blend of the two percentile ranks.

title: Holdout generalization check
note: Clustering has no test labels, but we can still hold out customers. The scaler and k-means are fitted on 80% only, then the unseen 20% are assigned. Similar silhouette plus a high ARI against a full-data fit means the segments generalize.

title: Transparent persona naming
note: Personas come from simple, auditable rules on the centroid (income vs population mean, spending score bands, age) rather than hand-labelling after the fact. Each persona maps to one concrete marketing action.

title: Serving: assign a customer
note: The saved scaler + k-means give the hard assignment; the Gaussian mixture gives soft membership probabilities, mapped onto k-means segment ids. A customer is flagged 'borderline' when the two nearest centroids are within 0.5 standard units.
